answer: The charge function was swept over gamma 0.75..1.50 (a 1.0 move costs the same at every point) on 2 panel(s), 3 arms, and the E230 deadband re-read at each gamma. The toll channel moves from -246.7 to -75.8 bp/yr and the pair from -793.3 to 239.0 bp/yr across the sweep. Selection is curvature-invariant in 6 of 6 arm cells (by construction -- it never touches the charge), so every cross-gamma move in the pair is the toll. 6 of 6 arms keep |t| >= 3.08 on the toll at ALL four gammas, and 6 of them keep the toll as the ONLY channel past the bar at every gamma. Arm ordering by pair is invariant on 1 of 2 panels. On the ladder, 9 of 12 (panel, arm, band) cells return the same verdict at every gamma; BAND_PAYS counts by gamma are 0.75: 2, 1.00: 1, 1.25: 0, 1.50: 0. E230's focus cell (primary_single / tilt_linear / f=0.10) reads BAND_PAYS@0.75 / BAND_PAYS@1.00 / BAND_NOISE@1.25 / BAND_NOISE@1.50 -- the verdict MOVES with curvature, so that cell is a finding about the cost model.

frozen_spec.bar_basis: two-sided 5% over 24 cells (arms x panels x gammas)
frozen_spec.charge: cost = cost_side_bp * |dw| ** gamma; a 1.0 move costs the same at every gamma
frozen_spec.const_weight: the base arm's OOS average weight at gamma=1.0, frozen across gammas so the rows stay comparable
frozen_spec.no_adoption: the arms are already judged; this asks only whether a conclusion is a fact about the cost model
frozen_spec.premise_note: a concave charge makes SMALL moves dearer per unit (0.5**0.75 = 0.594 > 0.5), so splitting one move into n steps costs sqrt(n) times as much, not less
